newsitem.title: USA: New York hospitals to get $1.25 bln in aid - NYT.
newsitem.headline: New York hospitals to get $1.25 bln in aid - NYT.

text.p: The aging hospitals of New York State are to get $1.25 billion in federal aid over five years, according to a deal struck between the state and the Clinton administration designed to help the hospitals reinvent themselves for the age of managed care, The New York Times said.

In Monday's edition, the paper said the aid package is part of an agreement that would for the first time require most of New York's 3.1 million Medicaid recipients to enroll in health maintenance organizations.
Critics call the deal a tax-payer bailout of a system that has refused to become efficient, the paper said.
Advocates say the deal will offer crucial support to public and non-public hospitals, many of them in New York City's poorer neighborhoods, the paper said.
